9: Model 2 is the blind mirror of model 1: it rebuilds the answer from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no candidate allele, gene or iteration-1 table allowed as an input until a final comparison step (a CI gate, tools/check_blind.py, enforces the declared inputs of every methodology entry). Six research steps, each with pre-registered hypotheses: (1) a symptom-only gene ranking (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented over HPO release 2026-06-23) produces a 404-gene target set in three tiers plus 396 length-matched decoy genes; its held-out recall@300 is measured on all 3,240 recessive diseases (0.335), so the set is treated as an enrichment, never as coverage. (2) A reference k-mer bait (every 31-mer of the 792 target and decoy genes, 2-bit packed, binary search behind a bitmap) selects from 1.07 billion reads the 14.7 million that touch those genes in one 50.8-minute server pass; minimap2 alignment; two small-variant callers with disjoint models (freebayes, bcftools call -m) and two structural-variant method classes (delly, dysgu); WhatsHap phasing; per-exon depth. Concordance with the vendor's genotypes is 0.9957 and 0.9927; 1,199 coding-adjacent alleles the vendor never reported are annotated. (3) An alignment-free, caller-free genotyper counts allele-specific k-mer pairs (381,510 probe pairs, 164,044 alleles) under a negative-binomial model fitted on 20,000 calibration markers, and a k-mer copy-number pass measures every target exon against a decoy null band. (4) A genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over every coding allele in the VCF with no hard filter: one calibrated lane per consequence class on the Tavtigian ACMG ladder (LOFTEE-style truncation rules, AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, ClinVar, gnomAD frequency, a non-PASS down-weight), a phenotype lane calibrated on step 1's own measured recall curve, and a STRING network lane for uncurated genes; 51,920 biallelic pair hypotheses over 11,465 genes, with two nulls (1,000-draw permutation of matched term sets; matched decoys through the same ratio) and a genotype-only ablation. (5) A knowledge engine over 815 genes (LitVar published alleles, PubTator gene-by-term co-mentions, UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold domain and confidence for each missense) judged against a PubMed hit-count baseline and matched decoys. (6) Reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60, fixed) of the routes that pass an admission rule (separates targets from decoys and reorders a trivial baseline); the read route confirms at weight 0; the ranking is hashed before the comparison, then a separate tool reads the pair to look for from iteration 1's committed selector file. Step 8 bounds mosaic aneuploidy per chromosome with two instruments sharing nothing past the FASTQ. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-2/).
10: Automated. The fused ranking and its rank-1 pair were produced and hashed (sha256 recorded in methodology entry 108) before any comparison with iteration 1 or with the confirmed answer. The submission file is built from coordinate-free selectors by tools: the rank-1 epcr is the register's suggested confidence for the anchor hypothesis, secondary rows sit below it by allele score, notes quote only columns of the warehouse table each allele was selected from, and the tool refuses a typed epcr, a typed note, or a digit inside a rationale. The submission layout (one primary pair, three secondary rows) follows a stated rule and was simulated against the scorer replica and the organisers' evaluation.py.
11: None on the candidate. Manual choices, all fixed before the runs and recorded in docs/iteration2/plan.md: the target-set cutoff (N = 300) and tiers; the fusion constant (k = 60) and the route-admission rule; the ACMG ladder values and the pre-registered cap of the AlphaMissense and SpliceAI lanes at 'moderate' (the mapping papers could not be fetched; the report names this the most load-bearing assumption); the secondary-finding rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). Two planned instruments were cut and recorded (ESM1b, an LLM evidence tournament); four named tools had no arm64 build and were substituted with a recorded reason. LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
13: GRCh38 no-alt + hs38d1 reference (195 contigs) for the bait, probes and alignment; Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF, coding regions) and VEP REST with gnomAD v4 frequencies, ClinVar classifications, AlphaMissense and SpliceAI; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF for the pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele catalogue typed in step 3; gnomAD v2 co-occurrence for P(trans) (GRCh37, bridged by dbSNP id); HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype); Phen2Gene and Monarch semsim REST as a second phenotype ranker; STRING v12 interaction partners (score >= 700); LitVar 2.0, PubTator 3.0, PubMed E-utilities; UniProt, InterPro, AlphaFold DB (per-residue pLDDT); UCSC cytobands for chromosome arms. Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256), and every derived table an edge in warehouse.data_lineage naming the delivered callset object and the clinical document by digest.
15: Pairs. Step 4 enumerates biallelic hypotheses per gene (compound heterozygous pairs, homozygous alleles, and single alleles as a separate shape) and ranks the pair, not the variant; step 6 fuses at the pair level; the primary row holds both alleles (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pair's phase could not be measured by the reads (no phase block reaches it) nor by population co-occurrence (undetermined); the trans configuration rests on the recessive model and on the oracle's reply to submission 1, and the report says so.
16: Three rows are marked finding_type=secondary, below the primary hit so they cannot lower F-max: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ClinVar P; ichthyosis vulgaris / atopy) and Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance thrombosis risk factor). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states are reported in iteration 1's report, not submitted. Iteration 2 also typed 88,754 ClinVar P/LP alleles alignment-free in the raw reads: 15 are present at heterozygous multiplicity across 14 genes, one of them the BUB1B stop; the others are listed in methodology entry 103 and were not promoted to rows, because four of the five confident ClinVar calls in target genes are an artefact of an over-tight fitted error rate (entry 096).
17: Two read passes ran on a small Linux server holding the 272-shard read store: the bait sweep over 1,071,835,104 reads in 50.8 minutes (4.2 hours projected on the laptop), and the k-mer dosage tally over 32 of 272 shards (124.5 million reads) in 2,803.8 seconds. Everything else ran on one arm64 laptop (16 GiB): bait build 51 s; k-mer genotype counting 765 s and copy-number counting 512 s over the baited reads; the 1,000-draw permutation null 34 minutes; the 3,240-disease phenotype benchmark about 2 h 16 min on one core; 5,705 PubTator searches and the LitVar/UniProt/InterPro/AlphaFold fetches against free public APIs; the fusion, unblinding, submission build and figure rendering in minutes. Storage: a hosted PostgreSQL (about 1.5 GB) and an object store for the reads. Cost: no paid compute; a small hosted database (about 5 euro per month).
18: We rebuilt, blind, the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA), a chromosome-instability disorder, after the challenge scorer had confirmed iteration 1's answer (BUB1B stop_gained + BUB1B missense) with a full match at rank 1. The question: was the pipeline right, or lucky? Iteration 2 started from the raw reads, the VCF and the eight HPO terms with no iteration-1 candidate or table allowed as input until a final comparison, enforced by a CI gate over every methodology entry's declared inputs. Six pre-registered research steps: a symptom-only target set whose held-out recall@300 was measured (0.335, not the 0.90 predicted) so it is an enrichment, not coverage; a reference k-mer read bait recovering 14.7 M of 1.07 B reads in one 50.8-minute pass, two independent callers reproducing the vendor's genotypes at 99.57 % and 99.27 % and reporting 1,199 alleles the vendor never did; an alignment-free, caller-free k-mer genotyper and copy-number pass typing 164,044 alleles, which finds both lead alleles at one copy each (posterior 1.0) and every BUB1B exon at two copies; a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking with no hard filter over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses in 11,465 genes, where the pair leads at ratio 341,019 (runner-up 1.70x behind and phased cis) and targets separate from matched decoys at AUC 0.706 [0.655, 0.751]; a knowledge engine over 815 genes, measured weak (AUC 0.634, gene rank 293 of 815); and a reciprocal-rank fusion frozen by hash before unblinding. The same two alleles came out first under both weightings. Strengths: replication by disjoint instruments, each with a measured error rate; every claim filed before its test with a refutation condition (40 hypotheses across steps 1-6 and 8, 16 refuted and reported); matched decoy nulls throughout; case-agnostic tools (k-mer bait and counting kernel, negative-binomial k-mer genotyper, calibrated LR pair ranker, RRF fuser with leave-one-out and freeze receipt, blind gate); coordinate-free selectors, so the submission rebuilds anywhere without a committed position. A second instrument bounds the disease's defining feature: no chromosome in the sequenced sample carries a mosaic aneuploidy above 2-3 % of cells (allele balance, 80 % power on 24 of 24 contigs, where the earlier statistic had power on none) or 1.6 % (k-mer dosage, X and Y recovered at one copy as the control). Limitations: one route carried the rediscovery (silencing the likelihood ranker drops the pair to rank 62; the symptom route had it at 9; the literature never listed it); the rank-1 position depends on the clinical terms and on one calibration cap; phase is unmeasured by reads or population data and rests on the oracle's reply; the read route has no ranking power of its own (targets and decoys equal, p = 0.589); four planned tools had no arm64 build; the mosaic bound concerns the sequenced sample only, with focal events invisible by construction. A second upload gains 0.000 bits on every expressible question, so this file is built and rehearsed on two scorers but held in reserve; 5 of 6 uploads remain.
